title: bien, bueno, ir: voy/va/vas/van, esta noche, carne, y

cards.title: Splits across Latin languages
cards.body: Italian sempre → siempre, bene → bien (well, as in bienvenido), French bon → bueno (good). Spotting the split helps new words stick.

cards.title: Work backwards from a form you hear
cards.body: From vamos (we go / let's go), the -amos tells you the key vowel is a. Take off the we ending and add the others.

cards.title: ir = to go (very irregular)
cards.body: Ir is two old verbs fused together, which is why its forms look so different. Full set: voy, va, vas, van, vamos.

cards.title: esta noche = tonight
cards.body: Literally 'this night'. Esta ends in a, which shows noche is feminine: la noche.

cards.title: Words ending in -e: check the context
cards.body: A word ending in -e could be either gender; look at the words around it or check a dictionary. Carne (meat, as in 'carnage') is feminine.

examples.en: I don't eat meat and I don't drink alcohol.
examples.es: No como carne y no tomo alcohol.
